question: Must this protocol-only stage show a compiled Android emulator/device roundtrip before merge, or should maintainers explicitly override real-behavior proof until the phone and watch endpoints land?
rationale: The patch deliberately has no runtime endpoint, so its current evidence cannot satisfy the external-PR real-behavior gate without either a small Android runtime harness or an explicit maintainer proof override.

options.title: Require Android runtime proof
options.body: Add redacted emulator/device or instrumentation output showing the compiled codec exchanges representative request, response, and event envelopes and rejects an invalid envelope.

options.title: Grant protocol-stage override
options.body: Explicitly accept focused unit, lint, and assemble evidence for this endpoint-free foundation and record a proof override before merge.

recommendation.title: Require Android runtime proof
recommendation.body: Add redacted emulator/device or instrumentation output showing the compiled codec exchanges representative request, response, and event envelopes and rejects an invalid envelope.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical issue and protocol commits show direct ownership of the staged architecture and its proof boundary.
